title: Which Indian city is ‘best’ for planned care? Start with the team, not a ranking
dek: Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and other clusters can all be relevant. A universal winner is not evidence-based.
imageAlt: Illustrative AI-generated referral journey connecting a fictional patient, home doctor and Indian care team.

sections.heading: There is no defensible single-city winner
paragraphs: A city does not treat a patient: a named clinical team, facility, and follow-up plan do. Public datasets do not provide risk-adjusted international-patient outcomes that support a broad city league table. We therefore do not label any city ‘best.’

A better short list starts with specialty fit and the named clinician’s current scope, then checks the facility’s accreditation status, capacity, communication, indicative plan, and continuity with the home doctor.

sections.heading: Use city as an operational filter
paragraphs: Large care clusters may offer more specialist choice and international connectivity, while a smaller city may offer a specific team or simpler local logistics. Neither trade-off is automatically superior.
bullets: Delhi NCR: broad multi-specialty cluster and a common international gateway.
Mumbai: major tertiary-care cluster; local travel time and accommodation location need planning.
Chennai: established hospital cluster; heat, language support and recovery logistics belong in the plan.
Bengaluru and Hyderabad: major clinical and transport hubs; verify the exact specialty team and facility.
Kochi and other regional centres: may suit a named service, but never infer capability from destination marketing.

sections.heading: A repeatable verification sequence
paragraphs: Search the current NABH directory by city and specialty, but treat accreditation as one signal rather than a guarantee of an individual outcome. Confirm the certificate scope and status directly, then ask the receiving team to answer the original referral question in writing.
